nodes/sol-review.json.description: Sol-only read-only adversarial audit of encryption/key availability table-state coverage
nodes/sol-review.json.promptTemplate:
You are GPT-6.1 Sol. Review in Japanese. Read results/reviews/sol-encryption-state-input.json and verify immutable snapshot hashes at start/end. Work only from this snapshot and explicit official specification evidence saved there; any new web lookup must be official MySQL only. This is focused design/coverage review, NOT final rollout approval.
ABSOLUTE: no source/results/file edits, DB connections, Docker commands, benchmark execution, delegation or workflow calls. File/hash reads and isolated pure computations allowed. Do not import modules with DB side effects. Main session19 author edits source and next runs WHITE all; do not inspect its growing outputs or assume snapshot is final source.
Latest user clarification: seed means encryption/decryption key, NOT RNG seed. User correctly rejects wording that sounds like TDE can work without any key. They require these to be table-state/condition coverage, rather than a new trivial observation that ciphertext cells can be counted.
Audit actual state taxonomy and evidence: unencrypted vs TDE healthy keyring vs TDE key unavailable, client key possession vs server decrypt capability, application-encrypted payload with unknown key vs encrypted/noninteger/UUID/composite primary-key designs vs opaque binary surrogate, storage-layer encryption vs encrypted file with no SQL access. Consider healthy-running service scope and what is meaningful to promise in key-loss states. Trace91,wide50/100,accuracy sampling and metadata and docs state catalog. No automatic demand for all combinations or physicalstorage test: explain which missing experiments can actually change a method decision. No keys/plaintext are necessary inputs to a SQL row counter when server can access table, but missing server TDE key cannot be bypassed. An engine may need MVCC access beyond nominal chosen secondary index; do not suggest indexes bypass TDE.
Independently assess owner coverage artifact; it is a hypothesis, not an approved diagnosis. Distinguish implemented/planned, historic measured, actual cryptographic fixture vs opaque bytes, official-specification only and unmeasured. Missing final all is expected, not a new finding. Is an actual application-crypto fixture/SELECT-only client test necessary to support current claims, or do row-count semantics and explicit width/index limits suffice? Is destructive missing-key experiment necessary, or can honest inapplicability/restoration precondition suffice? If necessary, propose disposable compose-only bounded design with no key removal from existing main data. No method/cap/scope reduction merely to pass.
Give concrete material findings only, stable IDs SOL-ENCRYPTION-STATE-001 etc, severity, scenario, exact snapshot file/function/line/claim, requiredCorrection and boundedRemediation. A doc-only misleading scope statement can be corrected without new all if measurement source remains unchanged. Do not overstate universal3/5/10% accuracy/no service impact. Preserve exactCOUNT vs metadata rough values vs conditional estimator distinction. Give a state coverage matrix and mandatory vs optional experiments with rationale. Return adapter JSON {"when":{},"payload":{...}} matching schema: decision accepted/rejected(DESIGN ONLY), guidelineSha256,reviewScope,findings,engineerQuestions,betterAlternatives,requestedExperiments,rolloutRecommendation,reviewEvidence,limitations,claimEvidenceMap,validationCoverageMatrix,priorityFixes. No files written. Final approval still requires actual all/owner audit/proof/two fresh Sol roles.
